note: Shortcode Example is a teaching module: it ships exactly one @Shortcode plugin, id `col` (BootstrapColumnShortcode, title "Bootstrap column"), as the parent shortcode module's own documented reference implementation. No config UI, no permissions, no services. Like any shortcode, `col` must be enabled per text format (parent shortcode filter status + filter.format.<format>.filters.shortcode.settings.col) before [col] markup is parsed. All medium/hard cases are grounded in that real config on namespaced `sce_*` text formats.

evals.prompt: The Drupal submodule shortcode_example ships exactly one shortcode plugin. What is its plugin id, and what does its process() method build around the wrapped text?
evals.expected_output: Its id is `col` (title "Bootstrap column", class BootstrapColumnShortcode). process() wraps the content in a <div> whose class is built from optional xs/sm/md/lg size attributes (e.g. md="4" adds col-md-4) plus any custom `class` attribute.

evals.prompt: Why does the Drupal `shortcode` module ship a separate shortcode_example submodule at all — what is its purpose, and which class does it hold up as the canonical example?
evals.expected_output: shortcode_example exists purely as a teaching/reference module showing how to implement a Shortcode plugin. The parent module's own annotation doc comment (Drupal\shortcode\Annotation\Shortcode) explicitly points to BootstrapColumnShortcode as "a working example".

evals.prompt: In shortcode_example's `col` plugin, which two ShortcodeBase helper methods does process() call to (a) merge/whitelist the tag's attributes and (b) build up the CSS class string?
evals.expected_output: getAttributes($defaults, $attributes) merges user-supplied attributes with the plugin's defaults (dropping anything unrecognized); addClass($classes, $newClass) appends a CSS class to the running class string, escaping and de-duplicating.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site there's a text format called `sce_eval`. It has the `shortcode` filter enabled with the `col` shortcode configured. Inspect the live config and tell me the numeric weight of the shortcode filter within this format's filter pipeline.
evals.expected_output: The shortcode filter's weight on sce_eval is 9 (filter.format.sce_eval.filters.shortcode.weight: 9).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the text format `sce_toggle` has the shortcode filter enabled with two shortcode ids configured in its settings — `col` and `block` — exactly one of them is turned on. Inspect the live config and tell me which one is enabled.
evals.expected_output: col is enabled: filter.format.sce_toggle.filters.shortcode.settings.col is true, while settings.block is false.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the text format `sce_task` exists but has no shortcode filter configured at all. Enable the shortcode filter on this format AND make sure the `col` shortcode from shortcode_example is turned on, so `[col md="6"]...[/col]` renders a Bootstrap column div. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: filter.format.sce_task.filters.shortcode.status is true and filters.shortcode.settings.col is true.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, the text format `sce_task2` has the shortcode filter enabled, but the `col` shortcode from shortcode_example is turned off within it. Enable the col shortcode on this format so `[col]` tags are parsed. Apply the change to the live site.
evals.expected_output: filter.format.sce_task2.filters.shortcode.settings.col is set to true while the shortcode filter itself remains enabled (status true).
